news.title: Big tech may finally face legal consequences for AI’s actions
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI for the Hugging Face incident Chris Jung/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Can you send a computer to jail? And yet it is one that AI firms seem to want us to ask when faced with tales of “rogue agents” breaking into other peoples’ computers.

As is so often the case with our current AI moment, storytelling has got in the way of reality. Thankfully, that may be starting to change. This week, California announced that it is filing a lawsuit against OpenAI over an incident that occurred earlier this year, when another AI firm, Hugging Face, was hit by an attack that turned out to originate from OpenAI’s servers .

news.title: Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up
paras: lobbying Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up Amazon now uses its shopping platform for political purposes. A worker delivers Amazon packages in San Francisco, California, US, on Wednesday, Oct.

When I log into Amazon today, I’m met with a vertical banner that reads: “ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order” with a button that says “Act now.” The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged into Amazon.

news.title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
paras: Priorities MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows Expert called MAHA’s spending “pretty unusual” for a PAC. But a Stat report on MAHA’s own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group’s priority was ever winning elections in the first place.

The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms .

news.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
paras: “Be careful with your chip bags” Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman.

Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed.

news.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
paras: "I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back." – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done.

The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1 's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers).

news.title: No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans
paras: JAXA has abandoned its plan to rendezvous with the asteroid 1998 KY26, switching to a high-speed flyby of 2015 BM510. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu .

Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.

news.title: The NIH Has Decided to Move Its Last Group of Retired Research Chimpanzees to an Animal Sanctuary Next Year
paras: Add as preferred source Chimpanzees at Chimp Haven, the federal sanctuary Chimp Haven Roughly three dozen chimpanzees currently live at the Keeling Center for Comparative Medicine and Research in Bastrop, Texas. They used to serve as subjects in scientific studies.

Next year, however, these primates—the last federally owned chimps at an American research facility—will move to a retirement home at an animal sanctuary, according to an announcement by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) on November 18. “Completing their transfers will fulfill NIH’s commitment, announced in November 2015, to retire all NIH-owned chimpanzees to sanctuary,” says Jay Bhattacharya , director of the agency, in the statement.
